text: Monte Carlo integration Monte Carlo integration estimates an integral as an expectation. Accuracy depends on the sampling distribution, weights and variance, not merely on using random numbers. Problem and representative equations Draw independent samples Xᵢ from a density p covering the support of f and average Yᵢ=f(Xᵢ)/p(Xᵢ). With finite second moment, estimate standard error by s_Y/√N. Algorithm Specify the distribution and random generator, draw samples and compute the weighted mean and variance. Importance sampling concentrates p where contributions matter, while monitoring heavy tails of f/p. Record generator/version, seed and sample count for reproducibility. Conditions and pitfalls The N⁻¹/² scale is statistical and conditional on assumptions such as independence and finite variance; it is not a deterministic bound for each run. Rare events and missed peaks can make variance estimates misleading. Correlated MCMC samples need a different uncertainty calculation. What to check Use repeated independent runs on known integrals to examine N scaling and interval coverage. Record actual mean error separately from estimated uncertainty, and verify that changes in importance density preserve the target integral.
